title: A graphene-based intelligent reconfigurable reflective surface for circularly polarized beam scanning in 6G applications
summary: Researchers present a graphene-based reconfigurable intelligent surface (CP-GRIS) for circularly polarized beam scanning in the sub-THz band. The 1-bit coding metasurface uses graphene modulation to switch two stable phase states, enabling dynamic 2D and 3D beam steering with low sidelobes. At 300 GHz the CP-GRIS achieves 24.8 dBi broadside gain, 4.4° beamwidth, and ±40° scanning with only 1.2 dBi scan loss, demonstrating promise for efficient beam manipulation in emerging 6G systems.
content:
This is an early access, unedited manuscript version provided to give prompt access to the findings. Before final publication the manuscript will undergo further editing and there may be errors that affect content; all legal disclaimers apply.

This paper presents a graphene-based reconfigurable intelligent surface (CP-GRIS) for circularly polarized beam scanning in the sub-THz range. The device is a 1-bit coding metasurface that combines phase tuning and polarization conversion in a compact structure to enable dynamic beam steering while maintaining low sidelobe levels.

Structure and operation: The CP-GRIS is composed of a 45×45 array (15 λ × 15 λ) of unit cells. Each unit cell consists of two inverted semilunar-shaped gold patches and an embedded graphene strip. The graphene strip produces a controllable 180° phase difference via current reversal, yielding two stable phase states with an approximate 180° phase difference across 266–332 GHz and a reflection magnitude above 0.85. By modulating graphene’s chemical potential and thereby changing its surface conductivity, the metasurface can switch between these two stable phase states, providing reconfigurability for beam control.

Performance and capabilities: The proposed CP-GRIS supports single-beam operation and full two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) beam-scanning capability. At 300 GHz the design achieves a maximum broadside gain of 24.8 dBi and a beamwidth of 4.4°. Beam steering is accomplished with sidelobe levels 15.3 dB below the main lobe at broadside, mainly due to the large electrical aperture and phase-controlled 1-bit coding. Compared with the feed horn antenna, the CP-GRIS produces a gain enhancement of 12.4 dBi. Beam scanning up to ±40° is demonstrated with a low scan loss of 1.2 dBi, highlighting the CP-GRIS as an efficient and versatile platform for sub-THz and THz beam manipulation and for emerging sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems.
